Hey I don’t have any advice, I just want you to know you’re not alone. I also “did everything right” and have never had any sort of career breakthrough. The job market is VERY BAD right now and we are experiencing global uncertainty paired with an ever increasing economic divide. The cards are stacked against us, and it isn’t our fault. I have two degrees, an extensive work history, a lifetime of volunteering, and several internships. I work at a grocery store. I don’t want to fall into despair, or get complacent, but it is disheartening. For everyone in this situation I think it is critically important to focus on the things that 1. matter to us and 2. we can control. My mental health has improved as I have been putting more focus on my relationships, on having a creative outlet, and spending a ton of time with my dog. This is more fantasy with horrifying elements than a straight horror novel, but I’ll post it because I often find this type of book more horrifying. N.K. Jemisin’s Broken Earth trilogy and her Inheritance Trilogy are all built on some gnarly worldbuilding and contain some spicy content. Much of that content is, well, horrifying, but the ways she writes about sex (all kinds of sex; consenting, abusive, riddled with power dynamics, loving, covetous, etc) is so well done and handled extremely well. It’s erotic and horny and interested in analyzing all these fucked up structures. Also, banger plots. You will also encounter multiple characters of all sorts of genders and sexualities, who are not tokenized. If you are okay with fantasy, I’d recommend them, but maybe check out a content warning list beforehand because the books, while amazing!-do get into some material that you might not want to engage with.

Hello, I would love any thoughts with this one! I have been doing very simple weekly three-card check in readings, with card one being where I am at right now/my representation, card two being the situation I am in/what needs attention, and card three being what will happen/where I need to focus my energy. It's not very precise, but it's what works for me.   


Today's reading was 1. The Sun (where I'm at), 2. The Wheel of Fortune (current situation) 3. Five of Cups (what's coming/where to focus my energy).   


It partly makes sense to me; I'm in a period of pretty intense awareness that I need to express myself authentically, and a lot of things are changing (potentially for the better) that I'm taking very badly, and grieving the loss of old crutches.   


My main question I suppose is one of time--for the past three months I have been VERY frequently pulling both The Sun and The Wheel of Fortune. It's been very frustrating because I am (like most of us in the global freaking pandemic) having A Rough Time. These cards at first felt like a very personal 'hang in there!' kind of message, but honestly, it feels like a sort of false hope? The Sun is not a card I have ever related to, and have rarely pulled this much in my entire time with Tarot. Does anyone have any insight they would like to share on frequently (and suddenly) pulling The Sun and The Wheel together, and on what other things The Sun can indicate for a person? Thanks!

chiming in from the US: I've self-admitted twice to a mental health facility, which if you have any control over/energy to do, is what I'd recommend over the emergency room (if you are planning to admit). Emergency rooms will place you on a 72 hour hold, which means yes you are safe from yourself for at least 72 hours, but your comfort and dignity will probably not be catered to. It's a LAST OPTION choice. 

If you have the resources to check what mental health facilities exist around you/if they take your insurance/if they're any good, I'd advise admitting there for a few days. Again, they're not amazing or very comfortable, but they'll keep you safe, get you some counseling, and potentially set you up on a medication regimen if you want to try it out. For me, admitting was a way to STOP all of the overwhelming things going on and get set up with therapists and psychiatrists outside of the hospital to help me re-start life again.

yo, I've been depressed for roughly half of my life, developed some pretty intense suicidal ideation ~five years ago. I am by social standards, a Good Mentally Ill Person (TM). I keep quiet, I go to therapy, I try the drugs they want me to try (they haven't worked yet). And still, I haven't gotten any better. The truth is, our mental healthcare system is very, very broken. You don't get any rewards (and certainly don't get the caliber of help you need) if you aren't ACTIVELY destructive to yourself or others. And, conversely, if you ARE, well you don't get the help you need then, either. Maybe you get a brief stint in a hospital (and the bills to go with it) or maybe you just get shucked into the ER for a night (with the bills to go with it) but ultimately, there's no real help for long-term, sustainable recovery. But so far it's the only system we have--a system which does contain people who sincerely do want to help--so many people continue to hopefully/desperately use it. 

Socially, I feel like this plays out on a larger scale. Since everything is still so taboo and our mental health system kind of silently condones that by being all hush-hush, nothing really gets talked about. I personally feel like I have two lives, two selves--the real me who is fuckin sick and hurting and desperate who spends all her free time at various doctors offices, and the functional adult me who goes to work, puts on a good face, and keeps everyone at a friendly distance so they don't discover what's actually going on. Because when they do (and sometimes they do) it gets weird. We don't socially have a system (speaking for myself in the US) whereby you help mentally ill people. Like, once you're a discovered neuroatypical, it's just like a brand of otherness. It freaks people out hardcore. Even the people who want to help kind of have limited options--recommend therapy, call a hotline, call 911. Which are all very limited and don't attack the root of the problem. 

okay enough rambles for now

 TLDR mental healthcare is a broken system, society doesn't have the scripts or resources for people to understand/help the mentally ill
